correctness.rationale: Both channels are CPTP: original Kraus completeness and nonnegative Pauli probabilities. Bloch matrices differ by b u v^T with v^T u=0 and both vectors in the lambda eigenspace of D, so M^n-D^n=n lambda^(n-1)buv^T exactly. On all (possibly entangled) inputs the difference is c_n B tensor partial-trace((A tensor I)X); trace duality bounds its diamond norm by c_n ||A||_infty ||B||_1, and the pure input in the v direction saturates. Adjacent-term ratio locates all optimal n; n(1-lambda)->s gives 2s exp(-s), with 2/e at the optimum. The standalone script has 75 exact-rational 3x3 power checks and finite-limit tests; these supplement, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: The two physical CPTP maps share every eigenvalue, making their exact optimal operational distinguishability a natural test of information lost by spectral description. The theorem gives a sharp ancilla-free experimental preparation/measurement, identifies every optimal step count, and shows a nonzero 2/e distinguishability despite one-step convergence to identity in the joint weak-noise/long-time limit. That persistent optimized effect, not a routine scalar computation or renaming of the source Jordan formula, motivates the fact. It does not claim adaptive multi-query superiority or higher-dimensional generality.
